subject: Feature packaging — unbundle vs retain, downgrade impact & pricing
content:
From: Eric Zhao <eric.zhao@novamed.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Procurement <procure@novamed.com>
Date: Sun, 4 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Feature packaging — plan options and downgrade impact

Hi David,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our engineering and product teams reviewed Redwood's serving options and we want to understand packaging tradeoffs before we commit. Two things we care about: 1) if we downgrade from Full tier to Compact tier later, what functionality and performance do we lose (esp. throughput, latency, and KV/prefix caching behavior), and 2) can we unbundle certain features (e.g., long-context KV cache and priority routing) as add-ons rather than in the main tier?

I've attached a short requirements sheet (NovoMed_requirements_20261004.xlsx) with our expected peak qps, typical sequence lengths, and a rough embedding volume. Can you help with:
- A clear matrix showing which features are included in Full vs Compact
- Quantified impact (percent latency increase, qps reduction) on typical workloads if we move to Compact
- Pricing paths for unbundling the KV cache and reserved burst capacity as add-ons

We also have procurement on copy. Looking for something we can take to our finance team to evaluate next week.

Best,
Eric
Eric Zhao
Head of Platform, NovoMed

---

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com>
To: Eric Zhao <eric.zhao@novamed.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Procurement <procure@novamed.com>
Date: Sun, 4 Oct 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Feature packaging — plan options and downgrade impact

Hi Eric — thanks for the spec sheet, that helps a lot. Quick summary up front: you can unbundle KV/prefix caching and reserved burst capacity as add-ons; the Compact tier is optimized for lower per-token cost at the expense of conservative batching and a smaller KV cache. Below I've sketched high-level deltas and next steps.

Feature matrix (high level):
- Full tier: 64GB KV cache, continuous batching, priority routing, SLA-backed latency targets, auto-fallback to model variant.
- Compact tier: 16GB KV cache, opportunistic batching, best-effort latency, no priority routing (requests are pooled into standard queue).
- Add-ons available: KV cache + reserved burst, priority routing, longer retention for traces/logs.

Quantified impact (based on the load in your sheet):
- Expected median latency increase on chat gen workloads when moving Full=>Compact: ~12-18% (95th percentile sees larger delta).
- Sustained qps capacity drop per shard: ~25-35% (depends on seq length distribution); for your median sequence length (~1,200 tokens) we estimate ~28% lower throughput without KV cache add-on.
- Embedding throughput unaffected by caching; affects cost if you rely on prefix reuse heavily.

Pricing routes:
A) Keep Full, lower unit rates with 12-month commit (recommended if you want stable latency).
B) Start Compact + add-ons (KV cache + burst) — lower entry price, pay as you add.
C) Start Full, commit 6 months, allow downgrade with 30-day notice and prorated credits for unused reserved capacity.

I'll pull together a short quote and a SKU split so you can show finance concrete numbers. Attaching a preliminary price workbook and SKU split for internal review.

Next steps:
1) Marissa — can you drop estimated list prices for the three SKU choices (Full, Compact, Add-on KV/burst) and a sample prorate calculation?
2) Eric — confirm whether you need the KV cache during peak windows only (makes a difference for burst addon sizing).

Thanks — talk soon.

—
David Kim
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment: Draft_Quote_placeholder.xlsx (see attachment in next mail)

Subject: Re: Feature packaging — plan options and downgrade impact

Hi team — adding a bit more color on practical packaging and the downgrade mechanics.

Operational recommendations:
- If NovoMed wants predictable app-level latency, recommend Full tier for the first 6–12 months while traffic patterns stabilize. Offer a 10% onboarding credit if they commit to 12 months.
- For customers who must start lean, we offer Compact + KV burst add-on that keeps latency within ~10% of Full during peak windows. This is priced as a reserved add-on (monthly) sized to expected peak qps.
- Downgrade path: full => compact is allowed with 30-day notice. Reserved capacity is prorated (we credit unused days), but any discounted committed rate is subject to a shortfall invoice if they terminate early.

SKU guidance (attached SKU_Splits_20261005.xlsx):
- SKU 1000-FULL: includes all core features, priced by committed qps + per-token.
- SKU 1001-COMPACT: base per-token lower; add-ons sold as percent uplift per month (cache=+18%, burst=+12%).
- Seat and support tiers remain separate line items.

Note on feature gating: we can gate KV cache behavior so that historical KV entries older than X are demoted; that reduces effective cache size without major infra changes (useful if they want a cheaper option that retains some cache benefits).

I attached a SKU split workbook with proposed price bands and an example proration table.

—
Marissa Cole
Director, GTM Pricing & Packaging, Redwood Inference

Attachment: SKU_Splits_20261005.xlsx

Thanks David and Marissa — this all helps. A few quick clarifications from our side:
- We like the Compact+KV burst path as a compromise but need a firm price for the add-on and the guaranteed burst capacity (number). Can you size the recommended reserved burst for our peak (as in the spreadsheet) and give a monthly line price?
- If we take Full now with a 12-month commit, what is the downgrade credit formula? The team is sensitive to early termination exposure — we want to avoid a large shortfall invoice if we need to scale down in 4–6 months.
- Would Redwood consider a stepped discount (e.g., 15% first 6 months, 10% months 7–12) as a middle ground to reduce our risk?

Procurement is asking for a single PDF quote they can circulate.

Regards,
Eric

Eric — thanks, appreciate the clear asks. Attached is a clean PDF quote (Draft_Quote_20261005.pdf) plus the SKU sizing workbook. Summary options in the quote:

Option A — Full (12-mo commit)
- Committed qps: 1,200 median (matches your sheet)
- Discount: 15% months 1–6, 10% months 7–12
- Early downgrade: allowed after month 3 with prorated credit for unused reserved capacity; shortfall calculation limited to difference between committed and actual usage over a 60-day lookback (designed to cap surprise invoices).

Option B — Compact + Add-ons
- Base Compact per-token: lower by ~22% vs Full per-token list
- KV cache add-on (reserved burst): sized for your 95th-percentile peaks; recommended monthly addon price: $4,500 (sized to ~2.5x baseline shard cache for peak windows)
- Priority routing addon: $1,200/month

Option C — Pilot (3 mo)
- Start Compact, enable KV burst only for peak windows (metered); conversion to Full triggers a 10% credit toward committed rate if converted within 90 days.

Next steps:
1) Eric — confirm which option you want us to pack into the PDF for procurement (A/B/C). If Option A, we'll push a DocuSign link for signature and calendar a tech handoff; if B/C we'll provide final sizing and a short playbook for switching tiers.
2) Marissa/Karthik — please confirm final list prices and authorize the credit language in Option A.

I've uploaded the quote to HubSpot and included the DocuSign link for the standard SOW clauses: https://redwood-docusign.example.com/DEAL-7643

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call if you want to run numbers live.
